item.title: MLB proposes salary cap delay. What teams would have to cut payroll?
item.description: Major League Baseball proposed Tuesday, Nov. 3 that a salary cap would be delayed by a year and implemented in 2028, permitting teams to operate knowing what the proposed rules would be in the upcoming Collective Bargaining Agreement. MLB proposed a $258.2 million salary cap and a $180.2 million floor, with MLB projecting that it would require 12 teams to increase payroll by $636 million to reach the floor, and eight clubs to decrease their payroll by $528 million to abide by the cap. MLB says that would net an additional $108 million payroll increase league-wide. The MLB Players Association has yet to issue a formal response, but the reaction continues to be vehemently opposed to anything that includes a salary cap, whether it’s next year or in the future, citing that the 2027 season would still limit spending since the CBT thresholds would remain unchanged. MLB also proposed increasing the minimum salary to $1 million for players with at least two years’ major-league service and $900,000 for those with less service; a $30 million increase to their pre-arbitration bonus pool, while also agreeing to the union’s proposal of lowering free agency from six years to five years for players 30 and older, while eliminating the qualifying offer system for free agents. “We recognize that clubs will need a full offseason to prepare to operate within the cap and floor system,’’ MLB said in a statement. “Therefore, with this offseason already underway, we proposed today to begin the cap and floor system in 2028. This proposal would allow a smoother transition into the cap and floor system without delaying key player benefits … and transactional reform that will reduce roster churn. “The projected salary cap and floor for 2028 continues to provide more money for major league players while leveling the playing field and giving more teams the ability to participate in the free agent market and retain their homegrown stars so that every fan believes their team has a fair chance to win it all.” If the salary cap and floor are implemented, the 12 teams that would have to increase payroll would be: the Miami Marlins , Cleveland Guardians , St. Louis Cardinals , Tampa Bay Rays , Washington Nationals , Chicago White Sox, Minnesota Twins, Colorado Rockies, Pittsburgh Pirates, Athletics, Cincinnati Reds and Milwaukee Brewers. The clubs that would have to lower their payroll: Los Angeles Dodgers , New York Mets, New York Yankees, Philadelphia Phillies, Toronto Blue Jays, San Diego Padres, Boston Red Sox and Chicago Cubs. MLB also said it would agree to allocate the players’ share of the 2026 CBT proceeds to players as a bonus based on service accrued in 2026 ($285,000 to each player that received a full year of service, $213,400 to any player with three-quarters of a year of service, $142,300 to any player with a half-year of service, and $71,100 for any player with a quarter year of service. item.title: Galatasaray end Stuttgart's unbeaten run, Sporting shine
item.description: Galatasaray players celebrate their side's first goal during the UEFA Champions League soccer match between Galatasaray Istanbul and VfB Stuttgart at Rams Park. (is associated with: «Galatasaray end Stuttgart's unbeaten run, Sporting shine») Mustafa Alkac/dpa VfB Stuttgart lost for the first time in the Champions League this season after Aleksei Batrakov scored twice in a 2-0 win for Galatasaray on Tuesday. The Germans threatened early on in the hostile Istanbul atmosphere when Jamie Leweling's shot came off both posts. But 14th-placed Gala soon went ahead when Jeff Chabot's mistake in the box was pounced on by Russian Batrakov, who fired into the top corner. The stadium speakers were quickly playing Russian music again when the 21-year-old nutmegged keeper Fabian Bredlow on 15 minutes. Chris Führich thought he had pulled one back, but video review spotted an offside in the build-up. Stuttgart remain in the top eight after four of eight league phase games, with a trip to Inter coming up at the end of the month. But Sebastian Hoeness' side can expect to slip out of the automatic qualification places for the last 16 once the rest of this week's games are completed. Sporting are fifth, three spots above Stuttgart, after a 1-0 win at Shakhtar Donetsk thanks to Issa Doumbia sweeping home. The 18th-placed Ukrainian side played their latest home game at Stamford Bridge in London. The Portuguese outfit look set to appoint Lyon's Paulo Fonseca as Rui Borges' replacement, but reserve coach Tiago Fernandes was in charge for this one. Seven games follow later on Tuesday, including injury-ravaged Bayern Munich at Atlético Madrid, holders and league leaders Paris Saint-Germain visiting Villarreal and under pressure Manchester United boss Michael Carrick hoping for an elusive win at home to Roma.

item.title: Spanish footballer De Miguel dies after collision with keeper
item.description: Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel was taken to hospital and placed in intensive care but his condition 'worsened neurologically' (Handout) Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel died on Tuesday as a result of injuries he suffered in a sickening collision with FC Andorra's goalkeeper in a Spanish second-division match, leaving football in mourning and condolences pouring in from around the globe. "Broken with pain, with a lump in our throat and unable to believe this is real, CD Tenerife announces the tragic death, at 8:00 am (0700 GMT), of Jesus de Miguel Alameda," his club Tenerife said in a statement. "No words can ease the pain, nothing can lessen this great feeling of sadness. Our thoughts are with the family, his close friends and Tenerife fans, who today are grieving over this terrible news." De Miguel, 30, was fouled in the middle of the pitch by Equatorial Guinea international goalkeeper Jesus Owono, who had raced out of his goal to try and clear the ball. Spanish police sources told AFP an investigation into what happened has been opened, under judicial supervision. The incident happened towards the end of the match at the Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez stadium, with the teams level at 2-2. Owono was sent off and the match was subsequently abandoned. Spanish media said that De Miguel suffered a cardiac arrest and was resuscitated. The player was taken to hospital and placed in intensive care, with Tenerife later saying that De Miguel's condition had "worsened neurologically", before his death. "I am so deeply sorry. Rest in peace, Jesus," former Barcelona defender Gerard Pique, Andorra's majority shareholder, wrote on social media. Andorra also sent their "most sincere condolences" to De Miguel's family, teammates and Tenerife. Tenerife president Felipe Minambres said his team would need professional help to recover from the tragedy. "We're unable to believe what has happened, but we will go through mourning, we will come together," the club chief told reporters. "We will need professional help, but also the support of all our fans, because they will share the same feeling that we have today." The club president said Tenerife's next two matches, against Granada on November 7 in the league and at Badajoz in the Copa del Rey on November 10, were set to be postponed following discussions with the Spanish football federation (RFEF). Real Madrid, Barcelona, Atletico Madrid and other clubs in Spain also sent messages of condolence, as well as the federation. The RFEF postponed all matches in the Copa del Rey and Copa de la Reina this week "as a gesture of respect and solidarity". European football's governing body UEFA said a minute's silence would be held before matches this week in the Champions League, Europa League and Conference League. - Messages of support - Real Madrid held a minute of silence before their training session on Tuesday. item.title: LeBron James takes a wine break after crashing into 76ers crowd
item.description: Who needs a Gatorade to quench your thirst when you can have a mid-game wine. Apparently, that's what Philadelphia 76ers star LeBron James figured during the Sixers' lopsided win over the Chicago Bulls at Xfinity Mobile Arena on Nov. 2. After battling for a loose ball, James found himself crashing into the South Philly crowd behind the basket and decided it was a good time for a break from the action. After bumping into a fan who was holding a cup of red wine, James jokingly grabbed the cup from the fan and took a sip before rejoining his teammates. Watch the video below. LeBron James take a wine break LeBron took a sip of a fan's drink mid game 😭 pic.twitter.com/1olB0GQ0ai — NBA on Prime (@NBAonPrime) November 3, 2026 We have found the best angle of the LeWineSip pic.twitter.com/ECV7gil8Ai — Philly Sports Sufferer (@mccrystal_alex) November 3, 2026 Sixers fans get a kick out of LeBron sipping wine Speaking with ESPN's Kris Rhim after having his cup of wine taken from him, fan Troy Clemons shared his initial reaction to the moment while dropping a strong line about James being a regular guy, according to a report by Fox News . "At the end of the day, he's another man like me," Clemons said when asked what he was going to do with the cup James drank from. "He's LeBron, but I threw that cup in the trash, and it's nothing up with him, but I just got a fresh drink." LeBron James stats with Sixers Along with his wine break, James also did his job on the court. In the 126-107 win over Chicago, James collected with 15 points, nine assists, seven rebounds and a steal while finishing a plus 30 in 31 minutes. So far in six games with Philly, James is averaging 16 points, seven rebounds, seven assists while shooting 45 percent from the field for a Sixers squad that holds the top spot in the Eastern Conference at 7-1. item.title: PFF: 5 lowest-graded Jets players on offense in Week 8 vs. Raiders
item.description: Scoring 33 points and still losing at home is a tough pill to swallow, particularly for a New York Jets team that desperately needed a victory. The 38-33 defeat against the Las Vegas Raiders marked New York's third consecutive loss and sixth defeat in its last seven games. When an offense produces that many points without getting the result, the postgame evaluation becomes more complicated. A five-touchdown afternoon isn't necessarily an indication that everyone performed well. Football is too dependent on individual assignments, execution and consistency for the scoreboard to tell the entire story. Some players can contribute to a productive offensive showing while still struggling in their own responsibilities, and those shortcomings deserve attention. That's where PFF's individual grades become useful. They offer another perspective on Sunday's performance and help identify areas where New York could have received better execution. With the Jets searching for answers, the less encouraging evaluations are worth examining just as closely as the standout performances. item.title: Where the Titans rank in key statistics heading into the bye
item.description: CINCINNATI, OHIO - NOVEMBER 01: Head Coach Robert Saleh of the Tennessee Titans celebrates play against the Cincinnati Bengals during the third quarter at Paycor Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) | Getty Images When the schedule first came out, the Tennessee Titans’ bye week looked like it was at the perfect time. Getting a week off close to the middle of the season is the best-case scenario. The problem now for the Titans is that Cam Ward and the offense are coming off the best game of the season. It would be really great to get back out there this week to see if they could keep that momentum going. The Titans have a tough schedule coming off the bye with two games against the 5-2 Jacksonville Jaguars in three weeks. Jacksonville looks poised to run away with the AFC South. The Titans probably can’t spoil the division title for the Jags, but it sure would be fun to hang a loss or two on them. As we head into the bye week, let’s take a look at where the Titans rank in some key stats: Offense Yards per game: 272.5 (31st) Passing yards per game: 173 (29th) Rushing yards per game: 99.5 (23rd) Points per game: 18 (28th) You didn’t need this post to tell you the Titans’ offense has been bad this season, but as I mentioned above, they looked like they found something in the loss to the Cincinnati Bengals. Defense Yards per game: 382.4 (31st) Passing yards per game: 258.3 (31st) Rushing yards per game: 124.1 (22nd) Points per game: 24.9 (19th) The defense has also been bad, and that was with Jeffery Simmons. While I have hope the offense can turn the corner, I don’t have any hope for defensive improvement this season. They are going to need to upgrade a lot of spots on that side of the ball in the offseason.

item.title: Pro Sports Owners Back GOP In Senate Battleground Races
item.description: This is part of a Front Office Sports series about sports spending in the 2026 midterm elections. Several key battleground races will decide control of the U.S. Senate on Tuesday. The Republican candidates in those elections have benefitted from hundreds of thousands of dollars in donations from major U.S. sports team owners, according to a Front Office Sports analysis of Federal Election Commission filings. Sports owners in the NFL, NBA, WNBA, MLB, NHL, MLS, and NWSL donated more than $350,000 to principal campaign committees for Republican Senate candidates in battleground states. Team owners in those leagues spent less than a fifth of that amount supporting Democrats in those same races. Political action committees affiliated with the Republican candidates also received hundreds of thousands of dollars from sports owners. Across the board, sports owners overwhelmingly gave to Republican Senate candidates over Democrats. The principal campaign committees for Susan Collins in Alaska, Jon Husted in Ohio, and Mike Rogers in Michigan received the largest total donations from team owners. Roy Cooper in North Carolina and James Talarico in Texas were the only two Democrats to receive more donations to their principal campaign committees from sports owners than their opponents—though Texas Republican nominee Ken Paxton received sizable donations from the sports world to outside PACs from the sports world. Some of the most prolific donors for these races among team owners were Los Angeles Kings and Galaxy owner Philip Anschutz, Broncos owner Rob Walton, Cleveland Browns and Columbus soccer owners Jimmy and Dee Haslam, Magic owners Richard “Dick” and Dan DeVos, and San Francisco Giants owner Charles B. Johnson. New York Giants chairman Steve Tisch, Seattle Seahawks owner Vinod Khosla, Minnesota Twins owner Jim Pohlad, and Chicago Stars owner Laura Ricketts all donated to support Democratic candidates in battleground states. Other sports figures—including Northwestern University donor Pat Ryan , Secretary of Education and former WWE president and CEO Linda McMahon, and Texas Tech booster Cody Campbell —donated to Republicans in several key races. These data points include donations given directly to a candidate’s campaign committee, as well as transfers that originated from other groups but were directed to the candidate. For example, Giants owner Johnson donated $500,000 to Grow the Majority, a Republican joint fundraising committee focused on electing House candidates. That money was split up into at least 13 campaigns, in addition to other PACs and committees. Joint fundraising committees are required to include their allocation formula in solicitations for money, but donors can designate their contributions to go to specific candidates of their choosing. For some Wolves fans, that news will inevitably bring one name back into the conversation: Molineux. Wolves supporters are growing increasingly frustrated. César Peixoto’s position is coming under increasing scrutiny, performances have left plenty to be desired, and calls for a change in the dugout have become increasingly difficult to ignore. Nuno Espírito Santo Sacked by West Ham: Could a Wolves Reunion Be on the Cards? For many, the answer is obvious. Why look elsewhere when one of the most successful managers in the club’s modern history is suddenly available? Nuno Espírito Santo still carries enormous affection at Molineux. He transformed Wolves from a Championship side into a team capable of competing in the Premier League and taking on some of Europe’s biggest clubs. Now, following his departure from West Ham, a return is bound to spark discussion. But would bringing Nuno back actually be the right decision? Or would Wolves be better off remembering his first spell for what it was rather than attempting to recreate something that might no longer be possible? Why Wolves Fans Want Nuno Back Wolverhampton Wanderers Manager Nuno Espirito Santo celebrates towards the Wolves fans – Credit, IMAGO / Action Plus It is not difficult to understand the attraction. Nuno’s first spell at Wolves was arguably the most exciting period the club has experienced in the modern era. Arriving in 2017, he immediately transformed the team’s fortunes, winning the Championship title with 99 points in his first season. That promotion was only the beginning. Wolves finished seventh in the Premier League in consecutive seasons, secured European qualification, and reached the Europa League quarter-finals in 2020. For a club that had spent years moving between divisions and struggling for consistency, it was remarkable. Nuno built more than just a successful team. He established an identity. Supporters knew what they were getting from his side. There was organisation, discipline, intensity, and a clear understanding of how Wolves wanted to play. item.title: Giants trade candidate: Jets RB Breece Hall
item.description: Breece Hall | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The New York Giants are widely thought to be in hot pursuit of Indianapolis Colts star running back Jonathan Taylor, hoping to get a deal done before the Nov. 10 trade deadline. Perhaps that deal would also bring the Giants veteran defensive tackle Grover Stewart. What, though, if that doesn’t materialize? Could the Giants turn to the crosstown New York Jets for the big-time running back Giants head coach John Harbaugh has clearly sought since taking the job? The Jets say they are not interested in trading Breece Hall . “We’re in the business of keeping good players and he’s one of our better players. So, Breece will still be here,” said Jets head coach Aaron Glenn. Still, plans change. The Tennessee Titans were adamant they were not trading star defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons — until the Chicago Bears made them an offer they could not refuse. Connor Hughes, who covers both the Jets and Giants for SNY TV, told me the Jets would have to be “blown away” by an offer to trade the 25-year-old Hall, a 2022 second-round pick. Hughes told me that the inclusion of a second-round pick in any trade package would likely cause the Jets “have a discussion about” moving Hall. Why it would work Hall doesn’t have the resume of Taylor, Saquon Barkley, or Derrick Henry. He has just one 1,000-yard season in four full years. Perhaps, though, that can be explained at least in part by the Jets going 24-52 during Hall’s tenure. You can’t run the ball when you are always chasing. The good part of that from an acquiring team’s perspective is that Hall has just 1,004 touches in the NFL and should have a lot of mileage remaining. The Athletic lists Hall as its No. 7 potential trade candidate , and the best potentially available back after Taylor. Harbaugh said this week that the Giants need to keep both the short- and long-term in mind with limited draft capital to deal from. At 25 and signed through 2028, Hall would do that. Why it wouldn’t work If it would take a first-round pick to acquire Hall, that is probably a bridge too far for the Giants. The other factor is health. Hall is expected back this week, but has missed five weeks with a right quad injury. The Giants would need to be sure Hall is ready to help them right away.

item.title: 10 takeaways from Oregon State’s loss at Fresno State
item.description: FRESNO, Calif. — Oregon State lost to Fresno State 38-22 Saturday night at Valley Children’s Stadium. Here are 10 takeaways as the Beavers prepare to host Texas State. 1. Reality check Two things can be true. Oregon State can still be ahead of schedule and on its way to a legitimately surprising season amid a massive rebuild, complete with a potent offense. Much of its success thus far came by pounding less talented teams and several of the worst defenses in the country. And where OSU was vulnerable was there to be exploited by teams like Fresno State, which has talent and good coaching. The Beavers are not a College Football Playoff team. That dose of reality doesn’t diminish what’s being accomplished this season. They’re simply not one of the two most talented teams in the Pac-12 right now. 2. Oregon State was outcoached JaMarcus Shephard and his staff were outcoached for definitely the first time in conference play and arguably for the first time this season. Matt Entz laid out in detail what Fresno State picked up from studying Braden Atkinson from his time at Mercer and Oregon State’s tendencies. Bye weeks also include self-scouting. Fresno State was more prepared for what OSU showed and particularly offensively the Beavers did not have an effective counter. 3. Self-inflicted errors can’t happen in games like this Winning on the road against a team with at least comparable (if not better) talent and coaching is a difficult task to begin with. It becomes a whole lot harder with six presnap penalties and allowing five sacks with two leading to fumbles. OSU absolutely could have led by multiple scores early if not for a false start negating Jake Reichle’s would-be touchdown, if Aeryn Hampton’s foot was in bounds and if multiple other penalties didn’t occur. That doesn’t even get into defensive miscues from missed tackles or over-pursuits. 4. The offensive line may have had its worst game Houston was more physically dominating than Fresno State, but that’s to be expected. Oregon State’s offensive line had a brutal showing nearly across the board, with sacks allowed by multiple players in one-on-one matchups. OSU’s rushing stats are skewed by the sacks and not nearly as poor as the final box score, but the bottom line is Fresno State won the line of scrimmage and it’s not a particularly stout group. 5. If there’s one piece OSU’s receiving corps is missing it is a target with the size and length of Freeman, which the Beavers are leaning on via their tight ends. But an outside target like him is hard to beat and he showed why. 6. item.title: How Oregon State turned a raw athlete into a starting linebacker
item.description: CORVALLIS — Two years ago, Jarrel Comer was a freshman at Tallahassee Community College and had not played competitive football since middle school. Now he’s a starting outside linebacker at Oregon State . Comer played basketball at Eastside High School in Gainesville, Florida, but began college as a regular student. He looked for opportunities to play sports again and football became the opportunity at Citrus College in California. He boarded a plane for the first time to take a cross-country flight to play football for the first time in more than four years. “I was willing to take that chance to get to where I am today,” Comer said. He had 58 tackles (8.5 for loss), including six sacks at the California junior college and got on the radar of linebackers coach Cort Dennison, then at Idaho. Dennison kept pursuing Comer at OSU, where he signed in January and arrived during the spring. item.title: Stuttgart left frustrated in Istanbul as Batrakov double proves costly
item.description: Stuttgart left frustrated in Istanbul as Batrakov double proves costly A ferocious atmosphere greeted Stuttgart at RAMS Park, with Atakan Karazor picking up a yellow card inside the opening minute after catching Mario Lemina in midfield. Despite the hosts' early intensity, Stuttgart almost took the lead in the eighth minute. Chris Führich and Maximilian Mittelstädt combined well down the left to find Jamie Leweling, whose effort remarkably struck both posts before bouncing clear. Galatasaray made the visitors pay four minutes later, as Jeff Chabot's attempted clearance fell to Aleksey Batrakov just to the right of the penalty spot, before the Russian fired past Fabian Bredlow, who got a strong hand to the ball but should perhaps have done better. Just three minutes later, Batrakov had his second, latching onto a pass from Davinson Sánchez before slipping the ball through Bredlow's legs to double Galatasaray's advantage. Stuttgart's miserable opening continued when Karazor was forced off through injury, with youngster Yanik Spalt coming on in his place, before Galatasaray nearly added a third in the 22nd minute, with Bredlow denying Batrakov his hat-trick and Viktor Osimhen firing the rebound over the crossbar. Tempers flared with around ten minutes remaining before the break, as Barış Alper Yılmaz sent Führich tumbling off the pitch, sparking a confrontation involving players and members of both coaching staffs. Führich, heavily involved throughout the half, came close to pulling one back in the 42nd minute, curling an effort toward the far corner after cutting inside Roland Sallai, only for Uğurcan Çakır to get a slight touch and turn the ball narrowly wide. In the second half, the intensity from the visitors increased, with Führich continuing to have a superb game down the left for VfB. Seeking control again, Galatasaray turned to Rafa Leao for their own energy on their respective left flank, but it was Stuttgart who remained in the ascendancy. The biggest moment yet for Die Schwaben came just after 75 minutes, when Deniz Undav rattled the bar from the middle of the box, before Führich found the net from range with a curling effort. However, the Stuttgart hope would be short-lived, with referee Chris Kavanagh announcing that the goal had been ruled out for offside against skipper Undav. item.title: Rachel Apa, a 24-year-old athlete, dies after collapsing during her first New York City Marathon
item.description: Runners take part in the New York City Marathon on Nov. 1. (Caleb Bowlin / Getty Images) Rachel Apa, a former Division I field hockey player and first-time marathon runner, died Sunday after she collapsed while participating in the New York City Marathon. She was 24. Apa experienced a “medical incident” during the race, according to marathon organizers New York Road Runners, and a bystander administered CPR until medical staff arrived. Staff continued with CPR and also used a defibrillator in their efforts to revive her. EMS transported Apa to Mount Sinai Medical Center, where doctors tried to save her life for more than six hours, her father, Steve Apa, told the New York Times . “We are deeply saddened by Rachel’s passing following running in Sunday’s race,” the Road Runners said in a statement. “Our thoughts and sincere sympathies are with her family, friends, and the entire running community.” According to multiple media outlets, the family was told by doctors that Apa had died of rhabdomyolysis — “a rare condition in which muscle cells break down and release a substance into the blood that can lead to kidney failure,” according to the Mayo Clinic . Marathon runners are listed as people that could be affected by the condition. Read more: Appreciation: Ross Newhan, Hall of Fame baseball writer for The Times, dies at 89 The Office of Chief Medical Examiner in New York did not immediately respond to an inquiry for this article. Apa spent four years with the Bucknell University field hockey team before graduating in 2024 with a degree in business administration. She made 42 starts in 63 overall games, compiling 40 points on 17 goals and six assists. A product manager at TE Connectivity who was pursuing an MBA at Charleston Southern University in South Carolina, Apa decided earlier this year to run the New York City Marathon as part of the Parkinson’s Champions team. “My grandfather was my role model growing up,” she wrote on the team’s fundraising page . “He taught me to stay active, push my limits, and embrace challenges, shaping my love for sports and movement. Later in life, he was diagnosed with Parkinson’s disease, and I watched as the disease slowly took away the freedom to move that he once loved so much. item.description: John Cena Debut's the John Cena Classic Championship during RAW at Barclays Center on November 2, 2026 in New York City. (WWE/WWE via Getty Images) With the Major League Baseball season over, the Houston Astros' ballpark will be bereft of baseball for the foreseeable future. In the meantime, one of wrestling's biggest stars will take the stage there. On Monday night, wrestling superstar John Cena announced he will participate in WWE's Survivor Series: WarGames event at Houston's Daikin Park on Nov. 28. Cena announced the news himself on WWE's Monday Night RAW. Cena said he will be in Houston to unveil participants in his upcoming John Cena Classic tournament on Dec. 14 at Walt Disney World in Orlando, Florida. .@JohnCena returns to #SurvivorSeries in Houston Nov. 28! https://t.co/uJfzJFATbp - WWE (@WWE) November 3, 2026 Cena, a 17-time WWE World Champion, revealed that Cody Rhodes will be the first big name to take part in the Cena Classic. But before the Cena Classic is the Survivor Series, one of WWE's "Big Four" events. In July, WWE and the Houston Astros announced that Daikin Park will host the Survivor Series: War Games event on Nov. 28 for the 40th annual edition of the event. WWE's WarGames matches center around multiple teams of wrestlers duking it out inside a steel cage, and are traditionally some of WWE's marquee events. Daikin Park will be the second MLB stadium to host a Survivor Series: WarGames event. Last year Petco Park, home to the San Diego Padres, hosted the Survivor Series and set WWE attendance records. This will be the first WWE Premium Live Event held at Daikin Park since the Royal Rumble in 2020. At the 2020 Royal Rumble, what was then-Minute Maid Park was transformed into a wrestling arena and hosted 41,715 spectators. The Nov. 28 Survivor Series will also be Cena's first Survivor Series in Houston since 2017, when he participated as a member of Team SmackDown. Cena had said he would be retiring at the Survivor Series last year, but clearly he has other plans. The match has implications for Cena's John Cena Classic Tournament because every star involved in the Survivor Series is a potential invitee. Roman Reigns has already been confirmed, and current WWE storylines point to a planned five-on-five match between The Bloodline and 946. item.title: Enzo Maresca Describes Football Calendar as 'Marathon' Amid Manchester City Fitness Concerns
item.description: Enzo Maresca Describes Football Calendar as 'Marathon' Amid Manchester City Fitness Concerns Enzo Maresca and Man City face RB Leipzig next up in a challenging fixture schedule. Maresca, who has won 11 of his 15 matches as Manchester City manager so far, will be looking to return to winning ways after a turbulent spell on the touchline. The Italian yielded an unprecedented seven-game win streak in the Premier League just two weeks ago, where a 3-2 win over Ipswich Town made him the first manager in the league’s history to win his first seven games in the dugout. That feat came following wins against the likes of Liverpool and Manchester United , but their UEFA Champions League clash with RB Leipzig on Wednesday offers a welcome chance for Maresca to end a three-game run in which City have failed to win in regulation time. First came a damning and avoidable defeat to Aston Villa away from home before back-to-back meetings with Brighton and Hove Albion , where success could only be found from a penalty shootout in the Carabao Cup before losing in the Premier League four days ago. Speaking ahead of his side’s meeting with Leipzig, Maresca revealed his thoughts on Manchester City ’s form, which has seen them struggle to yield positive performances in recent outings. “I said many times, this is not a short run. It's not a sprint, it's like a marathon, we need to think about 65 games and now, for me, it's very important to win games in the way we're trying to do,” the 46-year-old said. On his players’ fitness later on in the season, he added: “But it's also very important to arrive in February, March and April - when things are going to be more exciting - to have all of them fit." The last time City faced Leipzig was in 2023/24, when Pep Guardiola’s side came out on top of two meetings, first 3-1 away from home before winning 3-2 a week later at the Etihad Stadium. Unironically, Phil Foden scored in both games, and the 26-year-old will hope to continue his scoring run against the Bundesliga club after re-establishing some commendable form over recent weeks, which Maresca praised on Tuesday evening. “I see Phil day by day better and better for sure, 100%. I've already said many times that he is going to give us many things this season,” Maresca said. "We have many games in all competitions and 20 senior players, all of them very good. it's good to have competition between them. Phil and Rayan [Cherki] are more or less in the same position. The Tampa Bay Lightning star forward has requested a trade and has already been linked to the Habs by several hockey insiders. Much of that stems from Kent Hughes and his staff doing their due diligence, which doesn’t automatically signal serious interest. A general manager’s job is to understand player value, and that cannot be done without making calls. There’s also clear financial upside in linking high-profile Canadian teams like the Habs or the Toronto Maple Leafs to major rumours. item.title: Khaman Maluach breaks silence on his altercation with Draymond Green
item.description: Photo by Chris Coduto/Getty Images Khaman Maluach revealed that he did not make any illegal contact on Draymond Green prior to the Golden State Warriors player committing a hard foul on him early in the second half of the game. With the second half having just started, the Phoenix Suns had the ball, and Maluach was trying to take possession in the paint, with Green trying to defend him. The four-time NBA champion appeared to fall to the ground after the Suns’ center made contact with him. Just a second later, Green grabbed Maluach and threw him to the floor, resulting in a technical foul for the Warriors player. “I think it’s just a basketball play. Just out there playing basketball. Nothing against Draymond,” said Maluach to the reporters. Dillon Brooks came to check on Maluach and stop Green from trying to do anything further. However, the Warriors player got heated, and this led to a scuffle between Green and Brooks, with their teammates trying to separate them. “It says a lot about our team. See your big brother stepping up for me. Keeps us together and keeps us pushing throughout the whole game,” said Maluach when asked about Brooks coming to defend him. The scuffle between Green and Brooks led to both getting technicals, but as Green had already received one for the foul, he was automatically ejected from the game. Until that point, Green had only scored 4 points. With the entire second half still to play, the challenge had become harder for the Warriors. However, they had a huge third-quarter performance and scored 42 points before adding 23 more in the fourth quarter to take a 116-113 win This was the Suns’ fourth defeat of the season. They are now in the middle of a three-game losing streak and will be looking to get out of it as they face the Portland Trail Blazers on Wednesday.
